title: Wellness 2.0: Who Do You Want To Be?

sentences.en: Religions tell us they have the key to our best lives.
sentences.zh: 宗教告诉我们，它们掌握着过上最好人生的秘诀。

sentences.en: Advice columnists tell us how to solve problems in our relationships.
sentences.zh: 情感专栏作家告诉我们如何解决人际关系中的问题。

sentences.en: And airport bookstores are stuffed with tomes on how to grow rich,
sentences.zh: 机场书店里摆满了如何发家致富的鸿篇巨著，

sentences.en: manage our time better, and build effective habits.
sentences.zh: 教我们如何更好地管理时间、建立高效的习惯。

sentences.en: All these sources of counsel can teach us valuable skills
sentences.zh: 所有这些咨询来源都可以教给我们宝贵的技能，

sentences.en: such as planning, patience, and perseverance.
These can be vitally important to success.
sentences.zh: 这些对于成功至关重要。

sentences.en: But in a world overflowing with useful advice,
sentences.zh: 但在这个充斥着实用建议的世界里，

sentences.en: why do so many people feel stuck?
sentences.zh: 为什么还有这么多人感到迷茫？

sentences.en: One answer, many of us are pursuing goals
sentences.zh: 答案之一是，我们许多人所追求的目标，

sentences.en: that are misaligned with our own deepest values and preferences.
sentences.zh: 与我们内心最深处的价值观和偏好并不一致。

sentences.en: This week, in the latest installment of our Wellness 2.0 series,
sentences.zh: 本周，在我们的“健康 2.0”系列节目的最新一期中，

sentences.en: what psychology can teach us about choosing a meaningful path for our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨心理学如何教我们为人生选择一条有意义的道路。

sentences.en: When you're a kid, grown-ups ask you what you want to do when you're an adult.
sentences.zh: 当你还是个孩子时，成年人会问你长大后想做什么。

sentences.en: When you're a teenager, college counselors ask you what you want to study.
sentences.zh: 当你成为青少年时，大学辅导员会问你想学什么专业。

sentences.en: Once you join the workforce, managers ask you what your goals are for the next few years.
sentences.zh: 一旦你步入职场，经理会问你未来几年的目标是什么。

sentences.en: At every stage, we are really being asked the same question.
sentences.zh: 在每个阶段，我们其实都在被问同一个问题。

sentences.en: What do you want to do with your life?
sentences.zh: 你究竟想用自己的人生做什么？

sentences.en: At the University of Missouri, psychologist Ken Sheldon studies the science of knowing what to want,
sentences.zh: 在密苏里大学，心理学家肯·谢尔顿研究的是“知道自己想要什么”的科学，

sentences.en: how to set your sights on targets that will actually make you happy if you achieve them.
sentences.zh: 即如何锁定那些一旦实现就能真正让你快乐的目标。

sentences.en: Ken Sheldon, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 肯·谢尔顿，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm happy to be here.
I want to take you back to 1981, Ken.
sentences.zh: 我想带你回到 1981 年，肯。

sentences.en: You just finished college and moved to Seattle.
sentences.zh: 你刚大学毕业，搬到了西雅图。

sentences.en: You wanted to become a musician.
sentences.zh: 你当时想成为一名音乐家。

sentences.en: Rock musicians can be kind of flaky and unreliable, and we were all in our 20s,
sentences.zh: 摇滚乐手有时有点靠不住、不那么可靠，我们当时都二十多岁，
每个人都有不同的目标。
每个人都有点自我中心，

sentences.en: and they might not have been committed the way we thought that they were,
sentences.zh: 他们可能不像我们想象的那样投入，

sentences.en: or maybe the guitarist slept with the singer unexpectedly.
sentences.zh: 或者也许吉他手出乎意料地和主唱睡在了一起。

sentences.en: There's a lot of things that can just get in the way of having a smoothly functioning unit.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情都会阻碍一个团队的顺利运转。

sentences.en: We just weren't able to make the agreements and follow through with them that we would have needed to make real progress.
sentences.zh: 我们就是无法达成协议并切实履行，而这些本是我们取得真正进步所必需的。

sentences.en: I understand that at one point you were recording songs for a radio song contest,
sentences.zh: 我听说有一段时间你正在为电台歌曲比赛录制歌曲，

sentences.en: and things didn't quite go smoothly.
sentences.zh: 事情进展得并不是很顺利。

sentences.en: Yeah, I had recorded my tracks on the song that we were going to submit to this contest,
sentences.zh: 是的，我把我将要提交到这次比赛的歌曲的音轨录好了，

sentences.en: and I left for a weekend hiking trip, expecting that the bandmates would put their tracks down so we could send in the song the next Monday.
sentences.zh: 然后我离开去进行了一场周末徒步旅行，以为队友们会录好他们的音轨，这样我们就能在接下来的周一寄出这首歌了。

sentences.en: And I got back, and nobody had done anything, and it was very disappointing.
sentences.zh: 等我回来时，什么都没人做，这非常令人失望。

sentences.en: I remember walking in the rain.
sentences.zh: 我还记得自己在雨中漫步的情景。

sentences.en: It was Seattle, wondering what to do next,
sentences.zh: 那是西雅图，我琢磨着接下来该怎么办，

sentences.en: and coming to the decision that this was probably not going to give me a way to make a living,
sentences.zh: 并做出了决定：这可能无法让我谋生，

sentences.en: and that music, or at least this particular band episode, was not going to work out,
sentences.zh: 音乐，或者至少是这次特定的乐队经历，是行不通的，

sentences.en: and that I needed to get serious about maybe something else.
sentences.zh: 我需要认真考虑一下别的出路。

sentences.en: What happened to Ken, of course, has happened to millions of people.
sentences.zh: 肯身上发生的事，当然也发生在千百万人身上。

sentences.en: Maybe it's happening to you right now.
sentences.zh: 也许这正发生在你身上。

sentences.en: You set your heart on something, and then find the thing you wanted
sentences.zh: 你一心渴望某样东西，然后发现你想要的东西，

sentences.en: doesn't look anything like the thing you thought you wanted.
sentences.zh: 跟你原以为自己想要的东西大相径庭。

sentences.en: So Ken did what lots of us do.
sentences.zh: 于是肯做了我们许多人都会做的事。

sentences.en: He flailed around looking for something new.
sentences.zh: 他四处碰壁，寻找新的出路。

sentences.en: He signed up for a master's program.
sentences.zh: 他报名了一个硕士项目。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a program at Seattle University in Existential Phenomenological Psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是西雅图大学的生存现象学心理治疗项目。

sentences.en: That's a lot of syllables, but it is a certain tradition within existential philosophy and counseling psychology.
sentences.zh: 这个名字有很多音节，但它确实是存在主义哲学和咨询心理学中的一个传统。

sentences.en: It's a legitimate approach to helping people.
sentences.zh: 这是一种帮助人们的正当方法。

sentences.en: And I was very interested in that program, not so much because I wanted to become a therapist,
sentences.zh: 我对那个项目很感兴趣，与其说是因为我想成为一名治疗师，

sentences.en: but more because I've always just been very theoretically oriented,
sentences.zh: 不如说是因为我一直以来都非常注重理论导向，

sentences.en: and these were new ideas that I didn't understand that seemed like they might be very relevant
sentences.zh: 而这些是我不懂的新观点，似乎与这种对清晰感的寻找、对自我人生方向的寻找高度相关。

sentences.en: to this search for clarity, the search for what to do with myself.
sentences.zh: 同样的，肯在做我们许多人都会做的事。

sentences.en: Again, Ken was doing what lots of us do.
sentences.zh: 我们向外部世界寻求关于我们应该如何度过一生的问题的答案。

sentences.en: We looked at the outside world to give us answers to questions about what we should do with our lives.
sentences.zh: 肯对生存现象学心理治疗的涉足并没有持续多久。

sentences.en: Ken's foray into existential phenomenological psychotherapy was short-lived.
sentences.zh: 他寻找的答案并没有出现。

sentences.en: The answers he was looking for were not forthcoming.

sentences.zh: 我的同学们，我们形成了一个紧密的群体。

sentences.en: My fellow classmates, we formed a tight cohort.

sentences.zh: 而我学到的最主要的一点是，我觉得我寻找的答案

sentences.en: And the main thing I learned was that I didn't think the answers I was looking for
sentences.zh: 不会从那个知识领域中产生。

sentences.en: were going to come from that area of knowledge.

sentences.zh: 嗯，我再次停止了那项尝试。

sentences.en: Well, I once again stopped doing that.
sentences.zh: 我在第一年后就退学了。

sentences.en: I dropped out after the first year.
sentences.zh: 最后，我感觉自己卡住了。

sentences.en: And in the end, I felt kind of stuck.

sentences.zh: 我做的工作薪水不高，社会地位也不高。

sentences.en: The jobs I was working were not very well paying, very high status.
sentences.zh: 但我好歹是个杜克大学的毕业生。

sentences.en: But here I was, a Duke graduate.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我或许应该过得更好才对。

sentences.en: You know, maybe I should be doing better than that.
sentences.zh: 所以我经历了一段非常非常迷茫、不知道接下来该做什么的时期。

sentences.en: So I was in a sort of period of really, really not knowing what to do next.
sentences.zh: 除了不知道下一步该做什么，肯还觉得自己很不达标。

sentences.en: In addition to not knowing what to do next, Ken felt like he was not measuring up.
sentences.zh: 他感觉到外界对他和他的名牌大学学位抱有更高的期望。

sentences.en: He sensed the world expected more from him and his impressive college degree.
sentences.zh: 他对自己的期望也更高。
为了继续寻找答案，他报名参加了一个在 20 世纪 70 年代和 80 年代初风靡一时的研讨会。

sentences.en: Still looking for answers, he signed up for a workshop that was all the rage in the 1970s and early 80s.
sentences.zh: 它被称为埃哈德研讨会培训，即 EST 培训。

sentences.en: It was called the Erhard Seminar's training, or EST training.
sentences.zh: 是的，EST 培训是由韦纳·埃哈德创立的。

sentences.en: Yeah, the EST training was created by Werner Erhard.

sentences.zh: 他其实是一个推销员，读过很多关于最佳表现、沟通、什么是思维以及思维训练课程的书籍。

sentences.en: He was actually a salesman who read a lot about optimal performance and communication and what is the mind and mind training classes.
sentences.zh: 他把这些都尝试了一遍，然后创立了自己的版本，叫做 EST 培训。

sentences.en: He tried them all, and then he created his own version called the EST training.
sentences.zh: 这不是什么精神层面的东西。

sentences.en: And it wasn't a spiritual thing.
sentences.zh: 它实际上旨在训练你了解自己的思维并更好地控制它。

sentences.en: It was actually designed to train you to understand your own mind and to control it better.
sentences.zh: 我听说你曾经参加过这个培训，这是一个跨越两个周末、共计 60 小时的课程。

sentences.en: I understand that at one point you had this training with a 60-hour course spread across two weekends.
sentences.zh: 请给我描述一下这个课程。
发生了什么？你学到了什么？它是如何结束的？

sentences.en: What happened and what you learned and how it ended?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个培训的设置是这样的：你坐在一个大厅里。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, the way the training was set up, you'd be seated in a ballroom.
sentences.zh: 他们会租用一个酒店宴会厅，里面摆满了椅子。

sentences.en: They'd rent a hotel ballroom, and they'd have chairs lined up.
sentences.zh: 会有两三百人排排坐在椅子上。

sentences.en: And so there would be 200 or 300 of you lined up in your chairs.
sentences.zh: 然后培训师会走出来，会有志愿者拿着麦克风递给想要发言的人。

sentences.en: And then the trainer would come out, and there would be volunteers who would bring microphones to people to speak into when they wanted to say something.
sentences.zh: 培训师带领我们进行了各种探索、流程，

sentences.en: And the trainer led us through a variety of explorations, processes,
sentences.zh: 以及旨在向我们展示我们的思维是如何运作的、它们目前是如何失灵的，并训练我们更好地运用它们的活动。

sentences.en: activities designed to show us how our minds work and how they're currently not working and training us to work them better.
sentences.zh: 我听说这门课程保证在第二个周末结束时能让人获得启蒙？

sentences.en: I understand the course guaranteed enlightenment at the end of the second weekend?

sentences.zh: 这实际上是最吸引我的地方。

sentences.en: That was actually the thing that attracted me to it moSt.
sentences.zh: 我不确定自己是否需要自助培训，但那个保证启蒙的承诺让我着迷，我很想知道那究竟会是什么样子。

sentences.en: I wasn't sure that I needed a self-help training, but that promise of guaranteed enlightenment, I was fascinated to find out what that was going to be.
sentences.zh: 那么第二个周末发生了什么？

sentences.en: And so what happened the second weekend?
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时我们进行到第四天。

sentences.en: Well, so we're on day four.
sentences.zh: 那是第二个周末的星期天，气氛一直在不断积蓄，

sentences.en: It's Sunday of the second weekend, and it's sort of building and building, and you're getting closer and closer to the material that they really want to hit you with at the end.
sentences.zh: 你越来越接近他们最后真正想要灌输给你的核心内容。

sentences.en: And the moment of enlightenment was being told that this is it.
sentences.zh: 而启蒙的时刻就是被告知：就是这样。

sentences.en: I imagine this must have been something of a letdown for the 200 people in the hall.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，对于大厅里的 200 人来说，这一定有点让人失望。

sentences.en: Yeah, it sounds like a bait and switch almoSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，听起来几乎就像是一场挂羊头卖狗肉的骗局。

sentences.en: So after the trainer told us this, people were like, what do you mean this is it?
sentences.zh: 所以在培训师告诉我们这些之后，大家都觉得：什么意思，这就完了？

sentences.en: So in this period of your life, Ken, I think you went through what a lot of young people go through.
sentences.zh: 所以在你人生的这个阶段，肯，我想你经历了许多年轻人都会经历的事情。

sentences.en: You know, you've just graduated college.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你刚从大学毕业。

sentences.en: You're trying your hand at different things.
sentences.zh: 你尝试着各种不同的事情。

sentences.en: You're throwing darts at the wall.
sentences.zh: 你在盲目地四处碰运气。

sentences.en: There must have been a period in your life when it must have felt quite discouraging.
sentences.zh: 在你人生的某个阶段，一定感到相当沮丧。

sentences.en: Did thoughts of self-doubt go through your mind at this time in your life?
sentences.zh: 在你人生的这个时期，自我怀疑的念头有没有在你的脑海中闪过？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say that I've had a lot of self-doubt that I've struggled with.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以说我一直在与大量的自我怀疑作斗争。

sentences.en: But, you know, a big part of the self-doubt involves the knowledge that it's only you who is making the choices in your life.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，自我怀疑很大一部分源于这样一种认知：只有你自己才是在你的人生中做出选择的那个人。

sentences.en: And I wasn't sure that I was good enough to do what maybe I was capable of doing.
sentences.zh: 我不确定自己是否足够优秀，能够做到我可能具备能力去做的事情。

sentences.en: Adrift and uncertain, Ken asked himself what he wanted from life.
sentences.zh: 随波逐流、充满不确定性的肯开始问自己到底想要从生活中得到什么。

sentences.en: The master's program in existential phenomenological psychotherapy turned out to be a bad fit.
sentences.zh: 生存现象学心理治疗的硕士项目证明并不适合他。

sentences.en: The EST workshops were a letdown.
Ken had always enjoyed science and big ideas.
sentences.zh: 肯一直很喜欢科学和宏大的理念。

sentences.en: He decided to enroll in a PhD program in psychology.
sentences.zh: 他决定注册攻读心理学博士学位。

sentences.en: At first, this seemed like another mistake.
sentences.zh: 起初，这看起来像是又一个错误。

sentences.en: But several years into the program, a teacher came along who changed the way Ken thought about the question of what he should do with his life.
sentences.zh: 但在该项目中读了几年后，出现了一位老师，他改变了肯对“自己应该如何度过一生”这一问题的看法。

sentences.en: This wasn't probably until my fourth year that Robert Emmons arrived, and I was a little bit adrift up to that point.
sentences.zh: 可能直到我读第四年时罗伯特·埃蒙斯才来，在那之前我一直有点随波逐流。

sentences.en: But once Bob showed up, I recognized that the research he was doing was fascinating, and I really wanted to learn about it.
sentences.zh: 但自从鲍勃出现后，我发现他正在做的研究非常迷人，我真的很想了解它。

sentences.en: And so what he was doing was a new approach to studying personality, where instead of giving people a trait questionnaire, how extroverted are you, and how agreeable, and so forth,
sentences.zh: 他当时在做的是一种研究人格的新方法，不是给人们一份特质问卷来测测你有多外向、多随和等等，

sentences.en: he gave people a blank sheet of paper.
And he said, tell me what you're striving to do.
sentences.zh: 他说，告诉我你正在为什么而奋斗。

sentences.en: And so there would be, say, 15 blank lines, and the participant would write down, you know, 10, 15, as many as they wanted, things that they are striving to do in their life.
sentences.zh: 所以会有比方说 15 行空白处，参与者会写下——你知道，10个、15个，或者任何他们想写的数量——他们一生中正在努力去实现的事情。

sentences.en: And that really intrigued me, because it's what I had been trying to do my whole life, was figure out what to strive for.
sentences.zh: 这真的深深吸引了我，因为这正是我一生都在试图做的事：弄清楚该为什么而奋斗。

sentences.en: Observing how other people write down the things they were striving for gave Ken a crucial insight.
sentences.zh: 观察其他人写下他们为之奋斗的目标，给了肯一个至关重要的启发。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is a blank piece of paper, and people write things down.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一张白纸，人们在上面写下各种东西。

sentences.en: And if you think about it, how do we know, or how do they know, they're writing good stuff down?
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，我们怎么知道，或者他们怎么知道，他们写的是好东西呢？

sentences.en: You know, maybe they're just writing down what their mom told them, or their friend told them, or what society has told them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许他们只是写下了他们的妈妈告诉他们的、他们的朋友告诉他们的，或者社会告诉他们的东西。

sentences.en: And so it was only thinking later about, you know, what is the meaning of these goal statements people are giving us,
sentences.zh: 所以，直到后来我才开始思考，你知道的，人们给我们的这些目标陈述究竟意味着什么

sentences.en: that I started to wonder, what if they're writing down the wrong things?
sentences.zh: 以至于我开始琢磨：如果他们记下的东西本来就是错的呢？

sentences.en: The hard question Ken realized wasn't figuring out how to get where you were going.
sentences.zh: 肯意识到，这个艰难的问题并不是弄清楚如何到达你想去的地方。

sentences.en: It was in figuring out where you wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 而是弄清楚你到底想去哪里。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to find the answer to that difficult question.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨如何找到这个难题的答案。

sentences.en: Psychologist Ken Sheldon studies how we choose goals for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 心理学家肯·谢尔顿一直在研究我们如何为自己选择目标。

sentences.en: His research has found that we often select the wrong goals.
sentences.zh: 他的研究发现，我们经常会选错目标。

sentences.en: That is, we point ourselves in directions that don't ultimately lead to lasting happiness.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们前进的方向最终并不能带来持久的幸福。

sentences.en: An important reason for this era is that people don't have a good sense of what will make them happy.
sentences.zh: 造成这种现象的一个重要原因，是人们对究竟什么能让自己幸福并没有清醒的认识。

sentences.en: One of the main things we find is that people are not very good at all at knowing how achieving their goals will affect them.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的主要情况之一，就是人们完全不擅长预判达成目标会对他们产生什么影响。

sentences.en: They can have a completely off-base feeling that this goal, if I finally get it, is going to make all the difference for me.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会产生一种完全偏差的感觉，觉得这个目标如果最终实现，将会彻底改变自己的人生。

sentences.en: But then when we actually come back and measure their happiness later on to see how it's been affected or not affected,
sentences.zh: 但当我们过一段时间回访并衡量他们的幸福感，看看它是否受到影响时，
我们往往发现没有任何改变。

sentences.en: So one of the biggest reasons that you and others have found that people come up with the wrong goals
